Todd,

This might be a better question for the Shiny-Discuss <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shiny-discuss> mailing list. Do you see the same behavior when running the app with runApp()?

-Andy

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Todd <todd.w.s...@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, Jul 5, 2014 at 3:04 PM
Subject: [shinyapps-users] Why do images flicker in production, and what can I do to fix it?
To: shinyap...@googlegroups.com

Here's a pretty simple shiny app:

server.R

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  vals = reactiveValues(counter=0)

  output$graph = renderPlot({
    plot(runif(100), runif(100), main=paste("Counter:", vals$counter))
  })

  loop = observe({
    for(i in 1:10000) {
      x = runif(100)
    }

    isolate({vals$counter = vals$counter + 1})

    if (isolate(vals$counter) < 100) {
      invalidateLater(0, session)
    }
  })
})

ui.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  plotOutput("graph")
))

I've hosted this at shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, here's the URL: https://todd.shinyapps.io/testing-plot-flicker/

However, if you watch the counter go, a lot of the time it will jump by 2, 3, or 4, I've even seen as high as 8 on occasion. Why aren't all of those plots getting rendered? Is there a way I can tell shiny to wait for the plot to be rendered on the client before re-executing the loop? I would be willing to increase total runtime in exchange for a guarantee that all plots will be rendered

Todd

messages.subject_clean: error Command failed (1) installing shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
Gerardo,

I don't know off hand why this error happens, but we can try to narrow it down.

- Are you able to install other packages? Can you try installing a package with "install.packages" command, for example:

install.packages("shiny")

- If that works, can you try the following:

devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny")

- One possibility is the path to your temp directory where the package is first downloaded is causing problem. You could try setting your "TEMP" environment variable to a simple path such as "C:\temp", restart RStudio, and then try to install "shinyapps".

Thanks,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: Broad questions about Shiny, Shiny Open Source and Shiny Pro
messages.subject_clean: Broad questions about Shiny, Shiny Open Source and Shiny Pro
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shiny Team,

I have attempted to answer many of my questions on my own, but here are some critical questions I either uncertain of the answer or simply found conflicting info on various web sites.

Thanks in advance,
Stephen McDaniel
Freakalytics, LLC

With either Shiny Open or Pro

1) What web server is used? How do we patch-individual components or patches for all components from Shiny team?

2) Can I ensure that the R code is hidden from users of Shiny?
This is very important when using embedded database credentials.
Likewise, can I ensure that a user can't engineer an unauthorized connection to other data in the R session?

3) Maybe I am asking this question incorrectly, but what are the core chart types in ggvis today? (e.g.- bar, line, scatter, etc.)

With Open Source Shiny Server

1) Can more than one user interact with an application at a port concurrently?
Are they each waiting for the prior users requests to complete? (Suppose it takes 10 seconds to react to a request, 2 people make requests very close to each other, so it then takes ~ 20 seconds for both requests to complete?)  Or, can multiple R processes be spawned for same app?

2) As I understand it, "one R process is created for every Shiny application you deploy, regardless of the number of concurrent users."  So, if I publish 10 dashboards (apps), there is an R process per dashboard.  However, these die after a pre-defined time and restart when next requested?  Or, are they waiting in idle mode?

With Pro Shiny Server

1) Can I use any SSL Cert provider? Where is doc on adding SSL certs?

2) Can I make all apps run on the same port?

3) On the current pricing page it states 20 or 200 concurrent connections as limits for the 10k/25k price points.  However, on StcakExchange, a Shiny developer wrote, "We've seen the simplest apps seamlessly support hundreds of concurrent users on a single Shiny process (doable in the open source version)."  So, I find this confusing, is there a limit on the number of concurrent sessions per app, per server, something else?

4) Do Shiny Server Pro licenses fees stay at first year fee every year?  Most enterprise software licenses drop in later years (often 25%-33% and even up to 50% of first year.)

messages.body_plain:
It is absolutely possible, but as Chad was hinting at, your database has to be accessible from outside your environment.  When an app is pushed to the cloud, it will no longer be running on your machine, which means that it will need a way to get to the database.  Typically, that would mean that you need to have your database somewhere that is accessible over the internet.

Hope this helps.
-Tareef

devtools::install_github("rstudio/shinyapps")

Best,
Tareef

messages.body_plain:
Hi, this error stems mainly from the fact of not saving the scripts, or the files containing the R code, in UTF-8 encoding. This happens because usually this is not the default encoding of Windows Systems. Once you have saved the files in the wrong encoding, even after converting them to UTF-8 encoding, it is likely for the error you get to persist. This is because when you save the files in a different encoding, there may be characters that are not parsed properly, damaging the file. So, after converting your  files to UTF-8 encoding, you should look for strange characters, or characters that are not rendered properly, correct them, and everything should go fine.

I am amateurish with R :)

There is nothing in the docs :)  It is something I just started experimenting with to try and solve the problem that shinyapps bundles the directory (and sub-directories) when it pushes up to ShinyApps.io so you can't reference files that are not in there.

In your case, you would probably want to do something like the following from the directory that contains your ui.R and server.R:

> ln -s myUtilities ~/myUtilities

and change your source call to:  source("myUtilities/utilityfunctions.R")

Let me know if that works for you.

messages.subject: My Shinyapp isn't loading assuming that the process is killed due to app_idle time out ?
messages.subject_clean: My Shinyapp isn't loading assuming that the process is killed due to app_idle time out ?
messages.body_plain:
Here you find my project shiny app.

https://palatinaleon.shinyapps.io/CourseProject/

It read in some posts that the reason could be the app_idle time as the loading of the data takes too much time so the server assumes the app doesn't work and kills the process. How can ich modify this time out for deploying my App at shiny.server. Or do i have to set up shiny-server myself ? Where can i find a good instruction for Ubuntu as the installation instructions I found not really helped?

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Invalid multibyte string error, as soon as App deployed
messages.body_plain:
I opened one of the files that you tried to read using
RCurl::getURL():
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noobuseR/Datasets/master/UAEexpatForum.txt,
and there were garbled characters in it. You can search for 0087 or <U
on that page (Ctrl + F). <U+xxxx> is a sign that your raw files were
not saved with the correct encoding (presumably UTF-8). However, I do
not think this is the reason for the error (<U+xxxx> is pure ASCII
after all). Since your app involves quite a few packages that are
unavailable in my system and server.R seems to be non-trivial for me
to read through, it may take a while for me to install all of them and
start diagnosing the problem. Before I really do that, could you try
this blind shot in the dark?

  devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny@v/0/10/1-rc")

Then re-deploy the app. We have tried hard to solve the Unicode
problem in shiny 0.10.1
(https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/kT4GAm_FAYU),
and I'm not sure if it will solve your problem by chance...

BTW, now I understand your rationale of scan(textConnection()), and I would use

data <- getURL(..., .encoding = 'UTF-8')
data <- unlist(strsplit(data, '\n'))

Meanwhile, I believe Encoding(x) <- 'UTF-8' should be very rarely
used, unless you are absolutely sure x is encoded in UTF-8 **and** R
marks its encoding as "unknown". In most cases, you should use iconv()
or enc2utf8() or enc2native() instead to do the conversion, instead of
forcibly assigning an encoding. When dealing with text processing, it
is best to convert non-native encodings to the system native encoding
in advance, and enc2native() can be very useful in this case. If you
do not live in the Windows world, you can simply ignore all I said
here :)

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

OK,

poster on another thread pointed out my problem. I had included the install_github( 'wc14goals', 'mpodell' ) call in my server.R and ui.R files deployed to ShinyApp.io.

The proper way to do it is to install the github package locally with the latest version of devtools  (v. 1.5 as of this writing) and including only the library (package) and data(package) commands in my server.R and ui.R files. Removing the install_github command fixed the problem.

-Mike

OK I pared down the code and appear to have located the issue
Here is thebare bones  code with all the libraries I wish to have in my real app

One problem is adding the 'Rstem' package independently. This is not a problem to remove
The second is the 'sentiment' package which depends on tm and Rstem. If I remove it, the full app works (other than the aspects of the code I need it for)
I tried putting it at head of libraries loaded but that did not help with any deployment

So this appears to identify the exact problem but is there a satisfactory solution?

ui.R

# library(sentiment)
library(tm)
library(wordcloud)
library(httr) # this needs to be loaded after tm as other wise the content function is masked

library(rvest)
library(rlist)
library(pipeR)
 library(rCharts)
 library(colorspace)

library(XML)
#library(Rstem)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(

    ),

    mainPanel(
      dataTableOutput("summaryTable")

    )
  )

))

server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  data <- reactive({

    initURL <- "http://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2014/jul/24/fifty-shades-of-grey-trailer-review"
    inithtml <- content(GET(initURL),"parsed")

    tag <-inithtml[xpath("//*/div[@id='d2-root']/@data-discussion-id")][[1]][1][[1]]
    commentURL <- paste0("http://discussion.theguardian.com/discussion/",tag,"?orderby=oldest&per_page=50&commentpage=1#show-all")
    html <- content(GET(commentURL), "parsed")

    words <- html[xpath('//*[contains(concat( " ", @class, " " ), concat( " ", "d2-body", " " ))]//text()')] %>>%
      list.map(
           xmlValue(.,trim = TRUE) %>>% ## so need XML as well m piper The %>>% operator evaluates the function call on the right-hand side with the left-hand side object being the first argument
           strsplit("[^a-zA-Z]") %>>%
           unlist(use.names = FALSE) %>>%
           tolower %>>%
           list.filter(nchar(.) > 3L)) %>>%
           unlist %>>%
           table %>>%
           list.sort(desc(.)
                     )

    df <- data.frame(words)

info=list(df=df)
print(df)
    return(info)

  })

output$summaryTable <- renderDataTable({
  tbl <- data()$df})

})

Adding support for R-Forge is on our list of things to do, but isn't supported today yet unfortunately.

-Tareef

The file structures are the same--the second one just has more rows of data. The larger one gives an error, which I can read on the javascript console: "requesty (sic) body in temp file not supported." It does the same thing in Chrome and IE for me. Thanks for the kind words Andrew.  We should be adding support for BioConductor in the next 2-3 months.  Sorry it is a little vague still, we are working primarily on improvements to the reliability, scalability, performance and ease of use of the platform right now.  Some of those changes have already rolled out, others are coming in the next 3-4 weeks.  Depending on how it all goes, adding support for both BioConductor and R-Forge is something that we have heard the need for in the past.

-Tareef
